findings_and_bottlenecks.bottleneck: REA CLI `--duration-ms` Mandatory Sleep (15.0s per chunk)
findings_and_bottlenecks.mechanism: REA CLI FridaInstrumentationService unconditionally calls `await delay(input.durationMs)`. When duration_ms=15000, 15 seconds are completely idle waiting for the timer after the GUI hook has already detached in <5ms.
findings_and_bottlenecks.remedy: In a multi-chunk session, execute all chunks within a single session and tune duration_ms to ~2000ms (sufficient for GUI loop dispatch with 40x safety margin).

findings_and_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Per-Chunk Process Lifecycle (PowerShell + Node + REA + Frida Attach)
findings_and_bottlenecks.mechanism: Every chunk runs a distinct PowerShell process (241ms), recalculates 200MB game EXE hash (1378ms), spawns Node.js (800ms), and attaches Frida to PID 10404 (1870ms). With N chunks, this ~4.3s overhead is paid N times.
findings_and_bottlenecks.remedy: SessionBatchTransport attaches Frida ONCE and reuses the single session for N chunks.

findings_and_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Native Game Execution is NOT the Bottleneck (<5ms for 6 items)
findings_and_bottlenecks.mechanism: The actual memory reads, Native Setters, and byte verification take under 5 milliseconds total per chunk.
findings_and_bottlenecks.remedy: Preserve all existing safety, CAS, unchanged byte verifications, and journal invariants without modification, because native execution overhead is negligible.
